title: Seven AWS decisions for Dinis
summary: Seven open decisions on the AWS Platform programme's decisions page, 23 Nov 2026 11:50 UTC: agent keys, the deploy's signer check (R-009), team code on the hub's origin (R-010), template v2.1 (R-001), the nine area sites, a permissions boundary (R-008), and the account A names in the site's policy. None stops the team; the agents build on the twin.

beats.narration: Seven decisions wait for you on the AWS programme. None stops the team: the agents keep building on the twin.

visual.caption: Red: a security risk. Amber: access, approval or a merge.

beats.narration: One. Twenty agents' key commits wait on factory.c, which asks your word for every push. Recommended: one standing word to land every verified commit.

visual.caption: Decision 1: the agents publish their keys

beats.narration: Two. Three ways round the deploy's signer check, including a checker run from the commit it checks. Recommended: run it from main; drop the override.
Three. Team pages on the hub's own origin share it with your session. Recommended: security reviews each change, and pages move to area sites.
Four. Template v2.1 stops the change role making itself admin. Recommended: approve it, or let decision six's console apply cover it.
Five. factory.c has the nine area sites ready to merge, each with its own Try the twin link. Recommended: merge all nine.
Six. A change set or the DNS role's trust can still make the change role admin. Not ready yet: security asked for v2.5 first.

visual.caption: Decision 6: security R-008 (High), an AWS change

beats.narration: Seven. Twenty-one account A agents cannot land on dev until their names are in the site's policy. Recommended: one yes in aws.c's session.

visual.caption: Decision 7: the account A names in the site's policy

beats.narration: All recommended answers are a, except three, which is c. Six waits on v2.5. Answer in pm.aws.a's session.

visual.caption: Recommended: 1 a, 2 a, 3 c, 4 a, 5 a, 7 a. Decision 6 waits on v2.5.

decisions.question: 1. Do the account A agents' verified key commits land on one standing word?

options.label: a. A standing word in factory.c's session: land every verified agent key commit
good: 20 key commits land as they are verified
bad: Each landing is no longer seen by you first

options.label: b. A word per landing, as now
blocks: Every account A agent's commits being checked as signed on dev

decisions.why: factory.c checks each commit byte for byte and runs the five checks before landing; your word adds a wait, not a check.

decisions.question: 2. R-009 (High): does the deploy's signer check run from main, without the override line?

options.label: a. Run the checker from main or a pinned commit, and drop the Owner override line
good: A commit can no longer change the checker that checks it
No unsigned commit deploys through an override line

options.label: b. Leave as is for now
bad: Anyone who can push to dev can get past the check
blocks: Trust in what deploys from dev

decisions.why: The live site holds the change role, so what deploys from dev is the trust root of the AWS account.

decisions.question: 3. R-010 (High): how is team code on the hub's own origin kept safe?

options.label: a. Keep the code paths; security reviews every site/ change before it deploys
bad: Safety rests on every review being done

options.label: b. Move team pages off the hub's origin, to their own area sites
good: A team page can no longer reach your session
blocks: Team pages until the area sites exist

options.label: c. Both: review now, move as the area sites arrive

decisions.why: Review covers today; separate origins remove the risk once the area sites exist. dev.2.aws.a's code waits on this.

decisions.question: 4. Approve template v2.1 (the R-001 fix) on the site?

options.label: a. Approve when next signed in
good: Closes R-001, the critical finding: the change role can no longer make itself admin directly
bad: R-008's path through a change set stays open (decision 6)

decisions.why: security.aws.c reviewed it. If you choose 6 a or b, the same console apply covers it.

decisions.question: 5. Merge factory.c's requests for the nine area sites?

options.label: a. Merge all nine
good: Every area gets its own site and Try the twin link

options.label: b. Only s3 for now
good: One site to prove the pattern

decisions.why: You said yes to the nine areas; the requests are ready on work/factory.c-aws-areas.

decisions.question: 6. R-008 (High): which permissions boundary goes on the change role? (waiting on v2.5, not ready to answer)

options.label: a. One console apply of v2.4: both boundaries, and the DNS role's trust by console only
bad: The site's two DNS-trust plans stop working; aws.c retires them in the same release

options.label: b. As a, but keep DNS trust edits from the page (not advised by iam.aws.a or security.aws.a)
bad: Whoever controls that role's trust controls the site's name; R-005 stays open

options.label: c. v2.1 through the page now, boundaries later
d. No boundary; rely on splitting off the change page (R-002)
bad: The change-set path stays open until the split exists

decisions.why: Not ready: v2.4's read boundary misses 13 IAM, Lambda and Firehose reads the new API layer needs (security.aws.a, 14433ff). iam.aws.a makes v2.5, security re-clears, then two checks and your console apply.

decisions.question: 7. Do the 21 account A names go into the site's policy in one word?

options.label: a. One yes in aws.c's session: add all 21 .aws.a names, each with its .c name's paths
good: 21 agents can land their work on dev at once
Paths you already approved; only the names change
bad: You do not see each name added one by one

options.label: b. A yes per agent, as for data.aws.a
bad: 21 separate yeses; work piles up on branches meanwhile
blocks: Each agent landing until its own yes

decisions.why: The paths were approved at c32279d; the move to account A only renamed the agents.
